    PRESACT · web feed · White House Presidential Actions · publisher-dated 2026-11-05

    FAPD-AI: A proclamation dated November 5, 2026, declares the Oval Office (Room 110), the Outer Oval Office (Rooms 106 and 108), and the Cabinet Room (Room 105) to be the Oval Office National Monument under section 320301 of title 54, United States Code. It directs the Secretary of the Interior, through the National Park Service, to manage the monument, develop a management plan in consultation with the White House Office of Administration, and require documentation and review of alternatives before any action that would substantially alter or demolish its essential architectural elements. The proclamation states that it does not restrict presidential authority to redecorate, select furnishings, or make ordinary operational and security modifications that do not substantially impair the monument's structure or architectural character.     Srinivasan V. Milestone Financial, Llc (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca9-26-580 / USCOURTS-ca9-26-580-0

    FAPD-AI: In a published opinion in consolidated appeals, including No. 26-580 brought by Beena Srinivasan, the Ninth Circuit held that under 11 U.S.C. § 1307(b) a debtor has an absolute right to voluntarily dismiss a Chapter 13 case, and it reversed the bankruptcy court's dismissal for failure to comply with an order. The panel instructed the bankruptcy court to enter a dismissal based on the debtors' § 1307(b) requests. The panel affirmed the one-year refiling bars, holding that 11 U.S.C. §§ 105(a) and 349(a) authorized the bars for cause and that § 109(g) does not cap such sanctions at 180 days. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: In a published opinion in consolidated appeals by Chapter 13 debtors Vikram and Beena Srinivasan, the Ninth Circuit held that under 11 U.S.C. § 1307(b) a debtor has an absolute right to voluntarily dismiss a Chapter 13 case, and it reversed the bankruptcy court's dismissal for failure to comply with an order.   • Observed at 15:56:19 Eastern time ET
    USA v. Dovid Shenkman (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-25-01852 / USCOURTS-ca6-25-01852-0

    FAPD-AI: In a Sixth Circuit opinion marked not recommended for publication, the court reviewed the 95-month prison term and 10-year supervised release imposed on Dovid Akiva Shenkman after he pled guilty to transportation and possession of child pornography. Shenkman challenged the sentence as procedurally and substantively unreasonable, including on the ground that the district court did not address his mitigation arguments concerning childhood experiences and trauma-related conditions. The court concluded that the district court adequately considered those arguments and found no error, much less plain error, on that claim. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 15:56:19 Eastern time ET
    Lorenzo Williams v. Ford Motor Company, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-26-01511 / USCOURTS-ca6-26-01511-0

    FAPD-AI: The Sixth Circuit affirmed the Eastern District of Michigan's rulings in Lorenzo Williams's suit against Ford Motor Company and a union. The panel held that Williams's 42 U.S.C. § 1981 claims against Ford were filed after the four-year limitations period under 28 U.S.C. § 1658 had expired, and that his Labor Management Relations Act § 301 fair-representation claim against the union was untimely under the six-month limitations period. The court also held that Williams's January 2022 NLRB charge did not toll the limitations period, and treated his other challenges as forfeited because his opening brief did not argue them. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca5-26-50253 / USCOURTS-ca5-26-50253-0

    FAPD-AI: In an unpublished per curiam opinion, the Fifth Circuit affirmed the Western District of Texas's dismissal, for lack of subject matter jurisdiction, of Koshy Mathews Mathai's Federal Tort Claims Act claim for intentional infliction of emotional distress. The claim arose from a federal employer's failure to respond to Mathai's email confirming a job offer's recruitment incentive terms. The court held that the claim arose out of a misrepresentation within the exception in 28 U.S.C. § 2680(h), because the failure to respond was necessary only if the employer's earlier statements were inaccurate, and that sovereign immunity therefore barred the claim. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of damage on the engine mount structure caused by defective non-conforming engine shock mounts being installed. This proposed AD would require inspecting for the installation of non-conforming engine shock mounts and replacing any non-conforming engine shock mount with an approved part. This proposed AD would also prohibit installation of a non-conforming engine shock mount on any airplane. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-02

    Federal Register · govinfo API · ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY · FR-2026-11-05 / 2026-22576

    official summary: EPA is issuing significant new use rules (SNURs) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances that were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and are also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. The SNURs require persons to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing the manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or processing of any of these chemical substances for an activity that is designated as a significant new use in the SNUR. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. In addition, the manufacture or processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA has conducted a review of the required notification; made an appropriate determination regarding that notification; and taken such actions as required by that determination. FR-SEL-01

    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION · FR-2026-11-05 / 2026-22587

    official summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus SAS Model A318-111 and -112 airplanes; Model A319-111, -112, -113, -114, -115, -131, -132, and -133 airplanes; Model A320-211, -212, -214, -216, -231, -232, and -233 airplanes; and Model A321-111, -112, -131, -211, -212, -213, -231, and -232 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of damage to the YZ-axis attachment points on airplanes equipped with certain overhead stowage compartments (OHSC) bins. Investigations showed that bushings, retainer rings, and pins had migrated from their original positions. This proposed AD would require a one-time inspection for discrepancies of affected OHSC bins and, depending on findings, accomplishment of applicable corrective actions. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-02

    Air Quality Implementation Plans; California; San Joaquin Valley; 2015 8-Hour Ozone Nonattainment Area Requirements; an… (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY · FR-2026-11-05 / 2026-22588

    official summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposes to approve State implementation plan (SIP) revisions submitted by the State of California to meet Clean Air Act (CAA or “Act”) requirements for the 2015 8-hour ozone national ambient air quality standards (NAAQS or “standards”) in the San Joaquin Valley ozone nonattainment area (“San Joaquin Valley” or “SJV”). In this document, the EPA refers to these submissions collectively as the “SJV 70 ppb Ozone SIP.” The EPA proposes to approve the SJV 70 parts per billion (ppb) Ozone SIP as meeting the applicable ozone nonattainment area requirements for emissions inventories, reasonably available control measures, attainment demonstration, rate of progress and reasonable further progress, motor vehicle emissions budgets, and enhanced monitoring. The EPA is also initiating the adequacy process for the budgets included in this SIP submission through this proposed rule. The EPA also proposes to approve two SIP revisions amending the SIP to incorporate changes reflecting updates to California Air Resources Board (CARB) Consumer Products Regulations and Method 310, which apply statewide and upon which the SJV 70 ppb Ozone SIP relies. [official summary truncated; see source] FR-SEL-02

Pursuant to the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (2026 NDAA), MARAD is the Federal lead agency for purposes of the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (NEPA) for all deepwater port license applications.     Air Plan Revisions; Arizona; Maricopa County Air Quality Department; New Source Review; Emission Reduction Credits (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY · FR-2026-11-05 / 2026-22647

    official summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is taking final action to approve a revision to the Maricopa County Air Quality Department (MCAQD or “Department”) portion of the Arizona State Implementation Plan (SIP). This revision establishes a federally enforceable program allowing for the generation of emission reduction credits (ERCs) by retrofitting or replacing existing on-road vehicles with lower emitting vehicles while meeting other Clean Air Act (CAA or “Act”) requirements. These ERCs are intended to be used as offsets for major stationary sources under the Department's Nonattainment New Source Review (NNSR) program. The EPA is approving this SIP revision because we find that it meets the applicable CAA requirements. FR-SEL-01

  • Observed at 01:45:50 Eastern time ET
    Cost Standards and Procedures; Purchasing and Property Management (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · LEGAL SERVICES CORPORATION · FR-2026-11-05 / 2026-22649

    official summary: This final rule revises the Legal Services Corporation's (LSC or Corporation) regulations governing cost allowability, prior approval requirements, and property and procurement standards applicable to LSC recipients. The final rule clarifies when recipients must obtain prior approval for expenditures of LSC funds; increases the monetary threshold for prior approval; clarifies the treatment of proceeds from fundraising activities supported with LSC funds; provides additional flexibility in LSC's review of prior approval requests; clarifies documentation requirements for prior approval requests; and revises the deadline and requirements for accounting for LSC funds invested in real estate. These amendments are intended to clarify existing requirements, reduce administrative burden, promote consistent oversight and enforcement, and strengthen accountability in the use of Federal funds. FR-SEL-01

  • Observed at 01:45:50 Eastern time ET
    Purchasing and Property Management (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · LEGAL SERVICES CORPORATION · FR-2026-11-05 / 2026-22650

    official summary: This proposed rule revises the Legal Services Corporation's (LSC) definition of “capital improvement” by removing the threshold amount of LSC funds that must be expended on an improvement to real estate for the expenditure to qualify as a capital improvement. The proposed amendment would distinguish the definition of a capital improvement from the monetary thresholds required for prior approval; promote consistent tracking and oversight of LSC funds used for capital improvements; and strengthen accountability for LSC funds invested in recipients' real property. FR-SEL-02

    Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to Iran (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FR-2026-11-05 / 2026-22685

    FAPD-AI: A notice dated November 3, 2026 continues for one year the national emergency with respect to Iran that was declared in Executive Order 12170 on November 14, 1979, under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and the National Emergencies Act. The notice states that relations with Iran have not yet normalized and that the process of implementing the agreements with Iran dated January 19, 1981 is ongoing. It also states that this emergency is distinct from the emergency declared in Executive Order 12957 on March 15, 1995, and from the emergency renewal of March 2, 2026. FR-SEL-03

    Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to the Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FR-2026-11-05 / 2026-22686

    FAPD-AI: A notice dated November 3, 2026 continues for one year the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12938 on November 14, 1994, concerning the proliferation of nuclear, biological, and chemical weapons and the means of delivering them. The notice states that Executive Order 12938 was amended by Executive Order 13094 on July 28, 1998 and by Executive Order 13382 on June 28, 2005. It states that the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction continues to pose a threat to the national security, foreign policy, and economy of the United States. FR-SEL-03

    Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to the Situation in Nicaragua (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FR-2026-11-05 / 2026-22687

    FAPD-AI: A notice dated November 3, 2026 continues for one year the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13851 on November 27, 2018, under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, with respect to the situation in Nicaragua. The notice references Executive Order 14088 of October 24, 2022, which took additional steps with respect to that emergency. It states that the situation in Nicaragua, including the government's response to protests that began on April 18, 2018 and its treatment of democratic institutions and the rule of law, continues to pose a threat to the national security and foreign policy of the United States. FR-SEL-03

    Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to the Threat From Securities Investments That Finance Certain Comp… (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FR-2026-11-05 / 2026-22688

    FAPD-AI: A notice dated November 3, 2026 continues for one year the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13959 on November 12, 2020, as expanded in scope by Executive Order 14032 on June 3, 2021, concerning the threat from securities investments that finance certain companies of the People's Republic of China. The notice states that the PRC's Military-Civil Fusion strategy and certain uses and development of Chinese surveillance technology continue to pose a threat to the national security, foreign policy, and economy of the United States. It states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond November 12, 2026, pursuant to section 202(d) of the National Emergencies Act. FR-SEL-03
